common_name: Encore Autumn Ruby Azalea (Reblooming Dwarf True-Red Azalea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 4.5-6.0), humus-rich soil in partial shade with at least 4 hours of direct sun; Autumn Ruby is one of the smallest Encore cultivars, well suited to tight foundation beds and large containers.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 4.5-6.0), humus-rich soil in partial shade with 4-6 hours of direct sun to support dependable rebloom. Encore Autumn Ruby is a petite, slow-growing cultivar (patented as PP12110) covered each spring in small, single, true ruby-red flowers, followed by sporadic summer color and a second strong flush in late summer and fall. Its tight, upright-spreading habit stays proportionate in small accent beds and formal plantings without regular shearing. Keep the shallow root zone consistently moist with mulch and apply an acid-forming fertilizer after the spring flush to sustain the later rebloom cycles.

common_name: Encore Autumn Starburst Azalea (Reblooming Bicolor Coral-and-White Azalea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 4.5-6.0), humus-rich soil in partial shade with at least 4 hours of direct sun; introduced in 2021, Autumn Starburst is grown for its high-contrast bicolor blooms and compact mounding habit.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 4.5-6.0), humus-rich soil in partial shade with 4-6 hours of direct sun for strongest repeat bloom. Encore Autumn Starburst produces ruffled, single-to-double flowers with a coral-pink center and a bold white margin, opening in a heavy spring flush and then again in smaller bursts through summer and fall. Dark green summer foliage shifts to a bronze-purple cast in winter, adding cold-season interest beyond the bloom cycles. Water deeply during dry spells, maintain mulch over the shallow root zone, and fertilize with an acid-forming product after the spring flush to encourage continued flowering.

common_name: Encore Autumn Empress Azalea (Reblooming Upright Pink Azalea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 4.5-6.0), humus-rich soil in partial shade with at least 4 hours of direct sun; Autumn Empress grows more upright than many Encore cultivars, making it a good choice for taller foundation plantings and informal hedges.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 4.5-6.0), humus-rich soil in partial shade with 4-6 hours of direct sun for dependable rebloom. Encore Autumn Empress bears clear pink flowers over dark green foliage that takes on a bronze tone in winter, flowering heavily in spring with lighter repeat flushes into fall. Its upright growth habit sets it apart from more low, mounding Encore selections and suits it to foundation plantings and mixed shrub borders where extra height is useful. Water deeply during dry periods, keep mulch over the shallow, fibrous roots, and fertilize with an acid-forming fertilizer after the spring bloom to support later flowering.

common_name: Encore Autumn Sweetheart Azalea (Reblooming Soft Pink Freckled Azalea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 4.5-6.0), humus-rich soil in partial shade with at least 4 hours of direct sun; Autumn Sweetheart is valued for its pale, two-toned blooms that soften the look of a mixed border.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 4.5-6.0), humus-rich soil in partial shade with 4-6 hours of direct sun to support repeat bloom. Encore Autumn Sweetheart opens pale pink flowers so light they read almost white, flecked with lavender freckles near the throat, in a heavy spring display followed by lighter rebloom through summer and fall. The compact, rounded habit fits well into foundation beds, mixed borders, and large containers without frequent pruning. Water deeply during dry spells, mulch to protect the shallow root zone, and feed with an acid-forming fertilizer after the spring flush to sustain later flowering.

common_name: Koromo Shikibu Azalea (Purple Spider Satsuki-Kurume Azalea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 4.5-6.0), humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; Koromo Shikibu was named the American Rhododendron Society Azalea of the Year in 2015 and is grown for its unusual strap-petaled flowers.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 4.5-6.0), humus-rich soil in partial to full shade, since this cultivar's slower growth and fine hairy foliage benefit from protection out of hot afternoon sun. Koromo Shikibu is a distinctive spider-type azalea whose narrow, strap-shaped lavender-to-purplish-pink petals are spotted darker at the base, opening in great profusion in mid-spring on an upright, slowly spreading, mounding shrub. Small, hairy evergreen leaves take on a bronze cast in winter, adding cold-season interest to the informal, textured flower display. Water during dry spells to keep the shallow root zone evenly moist, and prune only right after flowering, since next year's buds form soon after bloom ends.
sources: North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

common_name: Red Ruffles Azalea (Ruffled Red Rutherfordiana Azalea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 4.5-6.0), humus-rich soil in partial shade; Red Ruffles is a Rutherfordiana-hybrid Southern Indica type long grown across the Gulf South for its heavy, ruffled spring bloom.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 4.5-6.0), humus-rich soil in partial shade, sheltered from harsh midday sun. Red Ruffles is an open, multi-stemmed, upright-spreading shrub that produces large, ruffled, single-to-semi-double light-red flowers with a darker red blotch in a heavy mid-spring flush, with little to no repeat bloom later in the season. Its narrow, dark green leaves hold color through winter, giving year-round structure to mixed shrub borders and woodland-edge plantings. Water deeply during dry spells while the shrub establishes, and prune only immediately after flowering to avoid cutting off next year's flower buds.
sources: North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

common_name: Rose Greeley Azalea (Fragrant Double White Gable Hybrid Azalea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 4.5-6.0), humus-rich soil in partial shade; Rose Greeley is an older Gable hybrid prized for scented flowers and reliable cold hardiness further north than many evergreen azaleas.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 4.5-6.0), humus-rich soil in partial shade with protection from hot afternoon sun. Rose Greeley, a Gable hybrid azalea, bears large, hose-in-hose, pure white double flowers with a faint chartreuse throat and a light fragrance uncommon among evergreen azaleas, blooming in a single heavy mid-spring flush. Its dense, mounding, evergreen habit and above-average cold hardiness make it a dependable choice for shaded foundation beds and woodland gardens in cooler parts of its range as well as the Gulf Coast. Water deeply during dry periods, keep mulch over the shallow root zone, and prune only right after flowering since next year's buds set soon afterward.
sources: North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox
